followups.action: Request the neurologist's exam notes and any EMG report documenting lower motor neuron signs (e.g., weakness, atrophy, fasciculations).
followups.why: Documented LMN degeneration by exam, EMG or pathology meets this criterion; no such evidence leaves it unmet.

followups.action: Request a neurologist exam documenting upper motor neuron signs such as hyperreflexia, spasticity or Babinski sign.
followups.why: Clinical evidence of UMN degeneration meets the criterion; its absence means he does not qualify.

followups.action: Ask the treating neurologist whether symptoms or signs have spread within the onset region or to new regions since onset 14 months ago.
followups.why: Documented progressive spread meets the criterion; a stable, single-region picture does not.

followups.action: Request the EMG/nerve conduction results, MRI imaging and differential workup records that excluded other causes of UMN/LMN degeneration.
followups.why: The criterion is met only if the workup shows no other disease explaining the findings.

followups.action: Ask the patient whether he is willing and able to give written informed consent for study procedures.
followups.why: Willingness and capacity to consent decides this criterion; the study team obtains the actual consent.

followups.action: Ask the patient about his ability to travel to the site (nearest is about 75 miles away) and to attend all study visits, and ask the investigator for their judgment.
followups.why: The criterion depends on the investigator's judgment that he can complete all procedures and visits.

followups.action: Order a peak inspiratory flow rate (PIFR) measurement, using the trial's inhaler-resistance device if the site requires one.
followups.why: A PIFR of at least 100 L/min meets the criterion; a lower value does not.

followups.action: Ask the patient whether he is sexually active with a woman of childbearing potential and, if so, whether he agrees to the required contraception.
followups.why: If not sexually active with such a partner, the criterion does not apply; if he is, agreeing to contraception meets it.

followups.action: Repeat the ALSFRS-R at the screening visit and again at Day 1 and compare the two scores.
followups.why: A drop of 2.5 points or more between screening and Day 1 excludes him; a smaller change keeps him eligible.

followups.action: Ask the patient and his neurologist about any other neurological disorder, memory problems or dementia, and consider a brief cognitive screen.
followups.why: A significant other neurological disorder or cognitive impairment that interferes with assessments excludes him.

followups.action: Ask the patient and his primary care clinician about any history of schizophrenia, bipolar disorder or other significant psychiatric illness.
followups.why: A significant psychiatric illness excludes him; none keeps him eligible.

followups.action: Order a 12-lead ECG to measure QTc and request any cardiology history.
followups.why: A QTc above 500 ms or other severe cardiac disease excludes him.

followups.action: Ask the patient and review his records for any history of torsade de pointes or serious arrhythmia.
followups.why: Any history of torsade de pointes excludes him.

followups.action: Ask the patient and his clinician about heart failure symptoms and diagnosis, and the functional class if present.
followups.why: NYHA class 3 or greater heart failure excludes him; class 2 or lower, or none, does not.

followups.action: Ask the patient and review his records for any heart attack or unstable angina in the past 6 months.
followups.why: A heart attack or unstable angina within 6 months before screening excludes him.

followups.action: Ask the patient about his experience with inhalers or breathing treatments and whether he has trouble using them.
followups.why: Difficulty taking inhaled drugs excludes him; no difficulty keeps him eligible.

followups.action: Have the site run a dry powder inhaler (DPI) trial or demonstration to see whether he can use and tolerate it.
followups.why: Inability to tolerate an oral inhaled powder via DPI excludes him; successful use clears it.

followups.action: Ask the patient whether he has taken any investigational drug or joined another trial in the past 30 days or 5 half-lives, whichever is longer.
followups.why: Any investigational product within that window excludes him; none clears it.

followups.action: Measure his body weight at a clinic visit.
followups.why: A weight of 32 kg or less excludes him; a higher weight clears it.

followups.action: Measure height and weight and calculate his BMI.
followups.why: A BMI below 17.5 or above 35.0 excludes him; a value in between clears it.

followups.action: Use the same height and weight measurement to confirm his BMI at the time of screening.
followups.why: A BMI below 17.5 or above 35.0 at screening excludes him; a value in between clears it.

followups.action: Order a liver panel including AST and ALT.
followups.why: AST or ALT above 3 times the upper limit of normal excludes him.

followups.action: Order a total bilirubin with the same liver panel.
followups.why: A total bilirubin above 1.5 times the upper limit of normal excludes him.

followups.action: Ask the patient and his clinician about any history of cirrhosis, liver cancer or active hepatitis, and check records for hepatitis serology.
followups.why: Any of these liver diseases excludes him; none clears it.

followups.action: Order a serum creatinine and calculate creatinine clearance by the Cockcroft-Gault method.
followups.why: A creatinine clearance below 45 mL/min/1.73 m2 excludes him; 45 or above clears it.

followups.action: Send the full record and new lab results to the study investigator and ask for their view on any disorder or abnormal result that could interfere with participation.
followups.why: This rests on the investigator's opinion; no significant disorder or abnormal lab in their view clears it.

followups.action: Confirm with the study site that the pregnancy exclusion does not apply because the patient is male; no test is needed.
followups.why: The exclusion applies only to pregnant participants, so it should resolve as not applicable for a male patient.

coordinator_email.body:
Dear Dr. Elmaleh,

We are screening a 54-year-old man with limb-onset ALS for PHENOGENE-1A. He lives near Sacramento.

He already meets these criteria: age in range, ALS diagnosis, onset 14 months ago (24 or fewer), ALSFRS-R 41, bulbar and breathing subscores above the cutoffs, FVC 82% predicted, and stable riluzole for 8 months. He uses no ventilation or oxygen.

Still open: documentation of upper and lower motor neuron signs, disease spread and the exclusion workup; PIFR; ECG and cardiac history; liver and kidney labs; weight and BMI; inhaler tolerance; psychiatric and neurological history; and prior investigational drug use.

We will gather these through his neurologist and local labs and send them as soon as they are available.

Could you tell us:
1. Which site is nearest to Sacramento and is enrolling? The San Francisco site lists no contact.
2. What pre-screening steps and records do you require?

Thank you,
Clinical trial matching team

You are the right age, your ALS started less than two years ago, and your breathing and daily function test well. We still need more information. Your care team will ask for some records, blood tests, a heart test, and a breathing test. We will also ask the study team where the nearest site is. Joining a study is your choice. You can say no or stop at any time.

Su equipo de atención pedirá algunos expedientes, análisis de sangre, una prueba del corazón y una prueba de respiración. También preguntaremos al equipo del estudio dónde está el centro más cercano. Participar en un estudio es decisión suya. Usted puede decir que no o dejarlo en cualquier momento.

twice with the same arguments; call one again only if its result was an error you can fix.

criteria." or "Writing the follow-ups and the email." Keep it to what you are doing next.

   patient name or identifiers; age, sex and conditions are enough.

   joining is their choice. Write `en` at a 6th-grade reading level: short sentences, everyday
   words, no jargon or numbers they would need explained, under 120 words. Write `es` as the

followups.action: Request the neurologist's exam notes and any EMG report documenting lower motor neuron signs (e.g., weakness, atrophy, fasciculations).
followups.why: Documented LMN degeneration by exam, EMG or pathology meets this criterion; no such evidence leaves it unmet.

followups.action: Request a neurologist exam documenting upper motor neuron signs such as hyperreflexia, spasticity or Babinski sign.
followups.why: Clinical evidence of UMN degeneration meets the criterion; its absence means he does not qualify.

followups.action: Ask the treating neurologist whether symptoms or signs have spread within the onset region or to new regions since onset 14 months ago.
followups.why: Documented progressive spread meets the criterion; a stable, single-region picture does not.

followups.action: Request the EMG/nerve conduction results, MRI imaging and differential workup records that excluded other causes of UMN/LMN degeneration.
followups.why: The criterion is met only if the workup shows no other disease explaining the findings.

followups.action: Ask the patient whether he is willing and able to give written informed consent for study procedures.
followups.why: Willingness and capacity to consent decides this criterion; the study team obtains the actual consent.

followups.action: Ask the patient about his ability to travel to the site (nearest is about 75 miles away) and to attend all study visits, and ask the investigator for their judgment.
followups.why: The criterion depends on the investigator's judgment that he can complete all procedures and visits.

followups.action: Order a peak inspiratory flow rate (PIFR) measurement, using the trial's inhaler-resistance device if the site requires one.
followups.why: A PIFR of at least 100 L/min meets the criterion; a lower value does not.

followups.action: Ask the patient whether he is sexually active with a woman of childbearing potential and, if so, whether he agrees to the required contraception.
followups.why: If not sexually active with such a partner, the criterion does not apply; if he is, agreeing to contraception meets it.

followups.action: Repeat the ALSFRS-R at the screening visit and again at Day 1 and compare the two scores.
followups.why: A drop of 2.5 points or more between screening and Day 1 excludes him; a smaller change keeps him eligible.

followups.action: Ask the patient and his neurologist about any other neurological disorder, memory problems or dementia, and consider a brief cognitive screen.
followups.why: A significant other neurological disorder or cognitive impairment that interferes with assessments excludes him.

followups.action: Ask the patient and his primary care clinician about any history of schizophrenia, bipolar disorder or other significant psychiatric illness.
followups.why: A significant psychiatric illness excludes him; none keeps him eligible.

followups.action: Order a 12-lead ECG to measure QTc and request any cardiology history.
followups.why: A QTc above 500 ms or other severe cardiac disease excludes him.

followups.action: Ask the patient and review his records for any history of torsade de pointes or serious arrhythmia.
followups.why: Any history of torsade de pointes excludes him.

followups.action: Ask the patient and his clinician about heart failure symptoms and diagnosis, and the functional class if present.
followups.why: NYHA class 3 or greater heart failure excludes him; class 2 or lower, or none, does not.

followups.action: Ask the patient and review his records for any heart attack or unstable angina in the past 6 months.
followups.why: A heart attack or unstable angina within 6 months before screening excludes him.

followups.action: Ask the patient about his experience with inhalers or breathing treatments and whether he has trouble using them.
followups.why: Difficulty taking inhaled drugs excludes him; no difficulty keeps him eligible.

followups.action: Have the site run a dry powder inhaler (DPI) trial or demonstration to see whether he can use and tolerate it.
followups.why: Inability to tolerate an oral inhaled powder via DPI excludes him; successful use clears it.

followups.action: Ask the patient whether he has taken any investigational drug or joined another trial in the past 30 days or 5 half-lives, whichever is longer.
followups.why: Any investigational product within that window excludes him; none clears it.

followups.action: Measure his body weight at a clinic visit.
followups.why: A weight of 32 kg or less excludes him; a higher weight clears it.

followups.action: Measure height and weight and calculate his BMI.
followups.why: A BMI below 17.5 or above 35.0 excludes him; a value in between clears it.

followups.action: Use the same height and weight measurement to confirm his BMI at the time of screening.
followups.why: A BMI below 17.5 or above 35.0 at screening excludes him; a value in between clears it.

followups.action: Order a liver panel including AST and ALT.
followups.why: AST or ALT above 3 times the upper limit of normal excludes him.

followups.action: Order a total bilirubin with the same liver panel.
followups.why: A total bilirubin above 1.5 times the upper limit of normal excludes him.

followups.action: Ask the patient and his clinician about any history of cirrhosis, liver cancer or active hepatitis, and check records for hepatitis serology.
followups.why: Any of these liver diseases excludes him; none clears it.

followups.action: Order a serum creatinine and calculate creatinine clearance by the Cockcroft-Gault method.
followups.why: A creatinine clearance below 45 mL/min/1.73 m2 excludes him; 45 or above clears it.

followups.action: Send the full record and new lab results to the study investigator and ask for their view on any disorder or abnormal result that could interfere with participation.
followups.why: This rests on the investigator's opinion; no significant disorder or abnormal lab in their view clears it.

followups.action: Confirm with the study site that the pregnancy exclusion does not apply because the patient is male; no test is needed.
followups.why: The exclusion applies only to pregnant participants, so it should resolve as not applicable for a male patient.
